title: Commit Message Hooks
description: Enforce conventional commits and commit message standards with commit-msg hooks.

data.text: The commit-msg hook validates the commit message after the user enters it but before the commit is created. It receives the path to a temporary file containing the commit message as its argument. Use it to enforce conventional commits, maximum length, and required prefixes.

Conventional Commits is a specification for commit messages that enables automated changelogs, semantic versioning, and structured release notes. The format is: <type>(<scope>): <description>. Common types include feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, and perf.

data.title: Commit-msg hook for conventional commits
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/commit-msg

COMMIT_MSG_FILE=$1
COMMIT_MSG=$(cat "$COMMIT_MSG_FILE")

# Conventional Commits regex
type="feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|build|ci|revert"
scope="\(\([a-zA-Z0-9/_-]\+\)\)?"
pattern="^$type$scope: .\{1,72\}\$"

if ! echo "$COMMIT_MSG" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
  echo ""
  echo "Invalid commit message format."
  echo "Expected: <type>(<scope>): <description>"
  echo "Types: $type"
  echo ""
  echo "Your message:"
  echo "$COMMIT_MSG"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

echo "Commit message valid."
exit 0

data.title: Use commitlint for robust validation
data.text: Writing regex-based commit message validation is error-prone. Use the commitlint tool, which implements the Conventional Commits specification fully and integrates with Husky.
commitlint is a tool that checks commit messages against configurable rules. Install it with the conventional-config preset for out-of-the-box conventional commits support.

data.title: Set up commitlint with Husky
data.code:
# Install commitlint and its conventional config
npm install --save-dev @commitlint/cli @commitlint/config-conventional

# Create commitlint config
cat > commitlint.config.js << 'EOF'
module.exports = {
  extends: ['@commitlint/config-conventional'],
  rules: {
    'type-enum': [2, 'always', [
      'feat', 'fix', 'docs', 'style', 'refactor',
      'perf', 'test', 'build', 'ci', 'chore', 'revert'
    ]],
    'subject-case': [2, 'never', ['upper-case']],
    'subject-max-length': [2, 'always', 72]
  }
}
EOF

# Add commit-msg hook with Husky
npx husky add .husky/commit-msg "npx --no-install commitlint --edit $1"

git add commitlint.config.js .husky/commit-msg
git commit -m "chore: add commitlint configuration"

data.text: The prepare-commit-msg hook runs before the editor opens. It can pre-populate the commit message based on the branch name, ticket number, or a template. This reduces friction while still maintaining standards.

data.title: Pre-populate commit message from branch name
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg

COMMIT_MSG_FILE=$1
COMMIT_SOURCE=$2
SHA=$3

# Only modify messages from git commit (not merges, squashes, etc.)
if [ "$COMMIT_SOURCE" = "" ] || [ "$COMMIT_SOURCE" = "message" ]; then
  BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)
  
  # Extract ticket ID from branch (e.g., feature/JIRA-123-description)
  TICKET=$(echo "$BRANCH" | grep -oE '[A-Z]+-[0-9]+' | head -1)
  
  if [ -n "$TICKET" ]; then
    # Prepend ticket ID to first line
    FIRST_LINE=$(head -1 "$COMMIT_MSG_FILE")
    echo "[$TICKET] $FIRST_LINE" > "$COMMIT_MSG_FILE"
  fi
fi

exit 0

items.question: Can I bypass commit-msg validation?
items.answer: Yes, with git commit --no-verify. Use this only for emergency cases. Regular bypassing defeats the purpose of the hook.

items.question: Does commit-msg run on merge commits?
items.answer: Yes, unless you configure it not to. Merge commits often have auto-generated messages that may not follow your convention. Use prepare-commit-msg to customize merge messages.

items.question: What is the difference between prepare-commit-msg and commit-msg?
items.answer: prepare-commit-msg runs before the editor opens and can modify the message. commit-msg runs after the user edits and saves, and only validates.

items.question: Can I use conventional commits without a hook?
items.answer: You can, but enforcement requires discipline. Hooks guarantee consistency across all contributors and prevent accidental format violations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: commit-msg validates the commit message after editing but before commit creation
Use commitlint for robust, configurable message validation
prepare-commit-msg can pre-populate messages from branch names
Hooks are bypassed with --no-verify — use sparingly
